addiction.label: Addiction
addiction.note: Impaired use of a substance or behaviour, argued here to be a dignity disorder.

agency.label: Agency
agency.note: The capacity to act and choose; what treatment aims to restore.

akrasia.label: Akrasia
akrasia.note: Acting against one's own better judgement; the essay's internal conflict of the addict.

artificial-intelligence.label: Artificial intelligence
artificial-intelligence.note: Computational systems that perform cognitive tasks; the technology context both the MH encyclical and Venite ad me speak into.

autonomy.label: Autonomy
autonomy.note: The rival grounding the seed article rejects — dignity as self-rule.

body.label: Body
body.note: The body as a theme. Distinct from `embodiment`, which is the claim that the person IS bodily — Barry listed both, so they stay separate.

capabilities.label: Capabilities
capabilities.note: Dignity grounded in a threshold of capabilities (Nussbaum, Sen).

dependence.label: Dependence
dependence.note: MacIntyre's dependent rational animal — dependence as normal, not as deficiency.

development.label: Development
development.note: Development in Sen's sense — freedom as both the end and the means of development.

dignity-disorder.label: Dignity disorder
dignity-disorder.note: The seed essay's coinage for impaired existential, moral or social dignity: impaired rationality, will, capacity to love, and body.

disability.label: Disability
disability.note: Disability and severe cognitive impairment as the test case for any capacity-based account of dignity.

discourse-theory.label: Discourse theory
discourse-theory.note: Habermas's discourse theory of law and democracy; not discourse ethics generally.

disease-model.label: Disease model
disease-model.note: The claim that addiction is a brain disease; the essay's target when it calls choice versus disease a false dichotomy.

embodiment.label: Embodiment
embodiment.note: The person as bodily rather than a mind inhabiting a body. See `body`.

faith-transmission.label: Transmission of the faith
faith-transmission.note: How the faith is handed on — evangelization and catechesis as encounter with Christ, especially under cultural change.

history.label: History
history.note: A history-of-ideas treatment of a concept.

human-dignity.label: Human dignity
human-dignity.note: Added by Barry's decision on 2026-10-12. The subject of the seed article and of three works in the seed list; without it the index could not answer its own question.

human-person.label: Human person
human-person.note: The person as bearer of intrinsic worth; the subject dignity is predicated of.

human-rights.label: Human Rights
human-rights.note: Rights discourse, including dignity as a legal ground of rights.

law.label: Law
law.note: Dignity in legal and constitutional reasoning.

literature.label: Literature
literature.note: Works of imagination cited for an image of the person rather than for an argument.

love.label: Love
love.note: The capacity to love as a criterion of dignity, and its impairment as a harm.

neuroscience.label: Neuroscience
neuroscience.note: The clinical and neurobiological literature the essay reads dignity through.

ontology.label: Ontology
ontology.note: Grounding an ethic in what the human being is, rather than in procedure or agreement.

personalism.label: Personalism
personalism.note: Reasoning from the person as the irreducible unit of value; the essay's method.

procedural.label: Procedural
procedural.note: Dignity secured by fair procedure rather than by a claim about what the person is.

rational.label: Rational
rational.note: Rationality as a mark of the person — and the point at which capacity-based theories of dignity exclude the non-rational.

recognition.label: Recognition
recognition.note: Dignity as something conferred or won in social relations (Honneth, Taylor).

relationality.label: Relationality
relationality.note: Dignity as constituted by relations rather than by what the being is.

responsibility.label: Responsibility
responsibility.note: Who answers for the impairment — the person, the family, or the society.

sacred.label: Sacred
sacred.note: The sacred as a category set against the merely biological or the merely social.

someone-and-something.label: Someone and something
aliases: the difference between someone and something
someone-and-something.note: Spaemann's distinction: a person is a someone, never a something.

substance.label: Substance
substance.note: The Aristotelian-Thomistic substance claim the seed article defends.

the-linacre-quarterly.label: The Linacre Quarterly
the-linacre-quarterly.note: Journal of the Catholic Medical Association; the venue of the addiction-and-dignity essay.

virtue.label: Virtue/s
virtue.note: Virtue as the locus of the moral life; virtue ethics in medicine.

worth.label: Worth
worth.note: Worth as distinct from dignity in Sulmasy's and Kateb's usage.
